title: Barbell Shrug
summary: Barbell shrug: lift the shoulders toward the ears. Upper traps 1. Very loadable; grip is often the limit.

muscles.why: The upper traps raise the shoulder blades (elevation); mid/lower help to steady them (0.4).
You hold the bar the whole set (0.3).

setup.text: Bar in a rack at mid-thigh height.
Overhand grip just outside the hips.

form_cues.why: Straight up, not rolled, is the trap's line.
Pausing at the top stops a bounce.
Straight arms keeps the work on the traps.

form_cues.cue: Use straps when grip fails first
form_cues.why: Lets the traps reach the end of the set.

bias_tweaks.effect: More time at the shortest point.

mistakes.text: Rolling the shoulders in circles instead of moving straight up and down.
mistakes.fix: Lighten the load until you can pause at the top.

misconceptions.myth: Rolling the shoulders works more of the traps.
misconceptions.reality: The upper traps lift the shoulder blades; rolling adds no load.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: The app adds no ramp-up sets here. If the muscle is not warm from earlier work, make the first set a little lighter.

Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 2 reps in reserve in the 10-15 rep range. Low-risk to push close to failure.
Pick the bar up from a rack at mid-thigh height.

alternatives.why: Dumbbells at the sides; freer path.
Machine shrug, no grip limit from balance.
Walking with heavy weights: grip and traps.

notes: Shrug variations have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
